title: Expert-based controllability assessment of control transitions from automated to manual driving
author: Naujoks, Wiedemann, et al.

steps.title: Set up rating materials
steps.instruction: Obtain the video footage of each take‑over situation and the coding sheet (Fig. 2) that lists coding events across the categories: braking, longitudinal control, lateral control, lane changes, communication with other road users, vehicle operation, and facial expression. Ensure the rater is trained on the TOC‑Rating scheme.

substeps.instruction: Load video file into playback software
Print or open the coding sheet

steps.title: Check for non‑controllable events
steps.instruction: Watch the video and determine whether a non‑controllable event occurred (e.g., collision or loss of vehicle control). If such an event is present, assign a rating of 10 (not controllable) and skip all subsequent steps.

steps.title: Assess safety‑critical status
steps.instruction: If no non‑controllable event, decide whether the situation was safety‑critical, i.e., the driver endangered themselves or other road users, creating a non‑acceptable risk (e.g., near‑crash). Assign a rating between 7 and 9 according to the level of criticality and intensity of driver intervention required.

steps.title: Evaluate take‑over quality
steps.instruction: If the situation is not safety‑critical, evaluate take‑over quality by identifying driving errors such as lane exceedances, insufficient securing, or inadequate speed. Assign a rating between 4 and 6 based on the frequency and severity of these errors.

steps.title: Identify imprecisions
steps.instruction: If no driving errors are observed, assess for imprecisions such as imprecise lane keeping or hesitant deactivation of automation. Assign a rating of 2 or 3 depending on severity and frequency.

steps.title: Assign final controllability rating
steps.instruction: If no imprecisions are found, the take‑over performance is perfect; assign a rating of 1.

steps.title: Record coded events and rating
steps.instruction: Document the final rating (1‑to‑10) and record all coded events on the coding sheet, noting the categories (braking, longitudinal control, lateral control, lane changes, communication with other road users, vehicle operation, facial expression) and their frequency/severity.
